rationale: The ground-truth concerns center on validation completeness/rigor and whether Ref2VA was actually tested; Y directly engages both threads (findings on the memory-model's conflated variables, the self-contradicting 'past eight GPUs' claim, the undersampled peak-memory methodology, the untested Ref2VA restart/OOM risks) with several claims independently verifiable from the diff's own numbers. X's four findings (numactl-flag formatting, README indexing, audio_reference format, dangling RTX-PRO-5000 reference) are valid and well-grounded but orthogonal to what the human reviewers actually pushed on, giving it much lower recall. Y's greater volume of highly specific code-citation claims can't all be externally verified, trimming its precision slightly below X's, but its relevance and depth clearly outweigh that.
